authority_order: Current skill-row fields govern section, taxonomy, retrieval, lifecycle, and human-confirmation relationships.
Current graph-node fields govern structural node identity and may narrow a skill row through a fail-closed non-retrieval projection override.
When duplicated lifecycle or support fields conflict, reconciliation selects the less permissive value.
When duplicated evidence-risk fields conflict, reconciliation selects the higher risk.
No reconciliation rule may create a fact, enable retrieval, expand a section allowlist, or authorize an external claim.

intentional_node_row_difference_rules.node_type: graph node taxonomy is authoritative when a skill row omits node_type or records skill_row while the registered graph node is skill
intentional_node_row_difference_rules.projection_behavior: retrieval-ineligible graph nodes use non_retrieval_identity even when a legacy row records a more permissive behavior; a missing row value may use the registered node behavior
intentional_node_row_difference_rules.external_claim_policy: retrieval-ineligible graph nodes use skill_projection_not_proof even when a legacy row records a more permissive policy; a missing row value may use the registered node policy

allowed_mutations: retire contradictory or row-exceeding graph edges
add row-derived section and policy edges
refresh edge semantic and lifecycle fields against reconciled authority
align duplicated activation, support, and evidence-risk fields conservatively
rewrite broken graph_hop_path values through existing registered edges
set disconnected active graph nodes to RETIRED
forbidden_mutations: add or delete a skill row
add or delete a graph node
add a fact identifier or evidence reference
delete or rewrite a legacy embedding artifact
